name: FINDER
abstract: This work studies how close current systems are to genuinely useful deep research agents. The displayed leaderboard uses the Checklist Pass Rate reported in the paper.
contributions: The paper cares about whether the research process is genuinely completed, not only whether the final answer looks plausible.
The page uses checklist pass rate because it matches the process-oriented evaluation design.
method: FINDER focuses on whether deep research agents can produce analyst-level reports rather than simple answers.
It introduces 100 human-curated research tasks together with 419 structured checklist items.
These checklist items standardize report structure, analytical depth, and factual grounding.
Based on around 1,000 generated reports, the paper also proposes the DEFT failure taxonomy.
The main finding is that current systems struggle more with evidence integration, verification, and planning than with task understanding.

metrics.name: Checklist Pass Rate
metrics.note: Checklist-based pass rate reported by the paper.

leaderboard_note: The primary leaderboard uses Checklist Pass Rate from the main table. The paper also reports other research-quality indicators, but this page prioritizes the most direct task-completion signal.
